All edge cases are explored and recorded. Here's where we've landed.

**So far, these feature flows are settled for the first version:**

1. **Save a link** — auto-fills title, description, icon, and a preview; you can correct them, add tags, and write a formatted note.
2. **Consistent tagging** — suggests tags you already use and reuses them regardless of capitalization, so no near-duplicates.
3. **Powerful search** — live, case-insensitive, across everything, with exact tags (`#tag`), phrases (`"…"`), and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`/parentheses.
4. **Click a tag to filter.**
5. **No accidental duplicates** — the same address stays one bookmark; you're offered the existing one to edit.
6. **Edit anything** — address, title, description, tags, note; updates in place.
7. **Open the page from anywhere on the card.**
8. **Unreadable pages** — save anyway with your own details, clearly marked "not preserved," with a retry.
9. **Empty states & clear-search.**
10. **Long text** — shortened in the list with Show more/less.
11. **Big collections** — sort (newest-first default) and 20-at-a-time with Load more, with counts over the whole result set.

Everything else you mentioned — **preserving a saved copy of the page (and PDFs), reading-status tracking, archiving, import/export, bulk actions, and preferences** — is recorded for later cycles and not part of this build.

This is the natural point to switch from exploring to **actually building it for real** (that's a role change on my side, so I need your say-so). 

**May I start implementing this scope as the working application?** Once you approve, I'll build it, verify it against everything we settled, and then bring it back to you for acceptance.
